items.title: 'Resilience' of Israelis as they mourn the loss of loved ones and 'the sense that we can be safe'
items.summary: Angela Diffley is pleased to welcome Dr. Danny Brom, Founding Director of METIV, the Israel Psychotrauma Center in Jerusalem. According to Dr. Brom, as Israelis and Jewish people around the world continue to mourn the largest loss of Jewish life on a single day since the Holocaust, their fundamental sense of collective security has also been shattered. What strikes him, however, is the resilience that exists alongside the grieving. How can individuals, communities and society rebuild a sense of safety without allowing fear to dictate the future? Yet, as Dr. Brom observes, “the war is still going on,” while political leaders speak of pursuing “the ultimate victory, which no one really knows what that is.”

Il Sud di Israele, alle prime luci dell'alba, veniva preso alla sprovvista: mentre dalla vicina Striscia di Gaza iniziava il lancio di razzi verso lo Stato ebraico, i terroristi entravano via terra in Israele, a piedi, con velivoli artigianali o motociclette, compiendo massacri nei kibbutz, assaltando anche un festival musicale , e uccidendo e rapendo chi trovavano lungo la loro strada. Ad oggi si stima che le vittime siano state oltre 1.200.
